owner.occupation: Scout for an Asia-focused indie game publishing fund

world.bio: Scout for an Asia-focused indie game publishing fund based in Singapore. Ex-producer, shipped four titles on mobile and PC before moving to the investment side. I play around 300 demos a year and sign maybe four. Publicly, the fund says it wants 'games that could only come from one place'.
skills_assets: Eight years in game production, familiar with Unity, Unreal and Godot pipelines
A shortlist tracker with about 900 demos logged, tagged by region, genre and team size
Relationships with festival organisers in Tokyo, Seoul, Jakarta and Shanghai
Authority to recommend signings to the fund's investment committee; checks of USD 80k to 250k
A collection of old Game Boy cartridges, useful as a conversation starter

projects.name: Autumn scouting cycle
projects.text: Between September and November I review submissions from the fund's open call and attend two festivals. This year I have so far played 160 demos. The committee has asked for fewer, better signings. The fund's brief for this cycle: a playable vertical slice, original art, original audio, and a team of at least three. Solo developers and art-only or music-only pitches are declined automatically at the first filter, which saves me time but sometimes hurts.

projects.name: Fund portfolio check-in
projects.text: Quarterly check with the six studios we backed last year. Two are on schedule, one is late by four months, one has lost its lead programmer. I am preparing the written update for the committee.

notes.text: Played 14 demos today on the train and at my desk. Eleven were competent forgettable roguelikes with pixel art. The other three had something: one set in a Penang wet market, one built around Balinese gamelan timing. I flagged them. The wet market one has no audio yet, which kills it for us.

Toddler 1 had a fever, toddler 2 decided 4 am was a good time to play. I slept maybe three hours. Tried to review a build at lunch and fell asleep with the controller in my hand. Training for the sprint triathlon is a joke at this point; I skipped the swim.

Committee call. Chair repeated, again, that she wants 'games that could only come from one place'. I defend this line in public, but honestly it is hard to operationalise. A game about a Korean grandma's kitchen is not automatically specific; a game about a Taiwanese temple festival can still read generic if the systems are generic.

Rejected a lovely art-only pitch today. The artist had a gorgeous set of Peranakan tile illustrations and wanted us to fund a game around them. No programmer, no design, no audio. Our filter auto-declines. I wrote a kind note and suggested she look for collaborators. I hate this part of the job.
Sunday: 10km easy run, 20 min on the bike trainer. My knee clicks. Bought a Game Boy Color Pokémon Silver cart on Carousell for $18, label damaged but battery still alive. My wife rolled her eyes.

Lunch with an old colleague now at a big publisher. He says the market for narrative games is saturated and nobody wants to pay for localisation. I said we do. He laughed and said that is why we survive on small cheques.

Spent the evening writing feedback emails. Nine declines, two 'keep in touch', one 'send us the next build'. People write back thanking me for declines, which is strange and kind. One dev from Manila wrote that nobody had ever told him why before.
Sleep tracker says 4h40m. The kids discovered the stairs. I have a festival in Shanghai in three weeks and I keep forgetting to book the hotel.

messages.text:
Mei: Can you take the toddlers Saturday morning? I have the dentist.
Me: Yes, but I have a demo session at 2.
Mei: That's fine, you'll be back by then.
Me: If I'm not, blame the traffic on the PIE.

Aiko: We have a few teams from Kyushu who are doing shrine-themed games. Interested?
Me: Very. Do they have audio?
Aiko: One does, the others are still looking.
Me: Send the list. We need at least three members and original assets.

Marcus: Your shortlist has too many solo devs.
Me: They're the interesting ones.
Marcus: Interesting doesn't ship. Cap them.
Me: Understood. I'll note which ones could be matched with teams.

Rizal: Hi Daniel, my team is two people, a programmer and an artist. Would you still look at our slice?
Me: Thanks for writing. This year the fund only signs teams of three or more with original audio. Honestly I'd love to see it, but it won't get past our filter.
Rizal: Thanks for being straight.

Priya: Triathlon in 8 weeks. You've done two swims in September.
Me: Kids.
Priya: Everyone has kids. Do one swim this week.

relations.about: Pragmatic, pushes for numbers, cares about team size because last year's solo signings were late.
Tokyo festival organiser who forwards promising regional teams.
Always says musicians deserve better access to the game side.

constraints: Fund policy: teams of three or more, playable slice, original art and audio
Cannot promise anything before committee approval
sensitive: Exhausted by toddlers, worried about his health
Sometimes doubts whether the 'one place' line is a real filter or marketing
Personal opinion that the auto-decline rule is too rigid
